title: 2-Room Apartment Prices in Bucharest: What You Pay in 2026
description: 2-room flat prices in Bucharest, 2026: from 107,500 EUR in new buildings with VAT, parking, and fittings. Real calculation with a Titan example.
descriptionLlm: Guide to 2-room apartment prices in Bucharest in 2026: starting from 107,500 EUR without VAT in new buildings, with 21% VAT, parking, and included features. Real example from Ilioara Residence, Titan-Dristor, District 3. Complete breakdown from list price to final payment.
keywords: 2-room apartment price bucharest, bucharest 2-room flat price, how much is a 2-room flat, district 3 2-room apartment, titan 2-room apartment
lead: You search for "2-room apartment price Bucharest" and dozens of listings pop up with vastly different numbers. Some seem low, others make you close the tab immediately. The issue is not finding prices, you find plenty of them. It is not knowing what each price includes. A 95,000 euro listing without VAT, without parking, without flooring, can end up costing more than a 107,500 euro flat with everything included. That is why you should look closely at the full total, not just the headline figure. Otherwise you run into unpleasant surprises. Really.

image.alt: Facade of a new residential building with modern balconies in an urban area

x: A 2-room apartment in a new Bucharest building costs between 107,500 and 136,500 EUR without VAT, with the difference determined by floor, orientation, and surface area. And no, that difference is not small at all.
The 21% VAT is mandatory, so the actual price starts at around 130,000 euros all in.
The features included in the price make the real difference: underfloor heating, triple-glazed windows, individual boiler. What is not included becomes your direct bill, honestly.

sections.h2: What the price of a new apartment actually means

blocks.x: Two 2-room flats can show a 30,000 euro price difference and actually cost the exact same. The difference lies in what is included in the total. In reputable new developments, the advertised price usually includes finishes, heating unit, and flooring. In others, you only get bare walls and basic utilities, with the rest billed separately. Out of your own pocket.

A simple question that saves you headaches: does this price include everything I need to move in, or do I need to set aside extra money for flooring, heating unit, interior doors, and other missing essentials? When comparing two listings, compare identical items. Otherwise, you compare apples to oranges and wonder why the final cost is so high.

At Ilioara Residence, for example, the price starting from 107,500 EUR without VAT includes full underfloor heating, 7-chamber Salamander triple-glazed windows, and an Ariston 24 kW heating unit. These are not asterisked add-ons, they are included in the price you see. Truly.

sections.h2: Real breakdown: from advertised price to total cost

blocks.x: Let us take the most accessible 2-room unit in a new development in Titan. The price without VAT: 107,500 euros. Add the 21% VAT and you reach approximately 130,075 euros. That is the baseline figure you start with.

Then comes parking. A single spot costs 20,000 euros plus VAT, while a double Klauss system, two stacked cars, is 25,000 euros plus VAT. Not everyone buys parking right away, but it is wise to know the cost upfront, rather than discovering a lack of street parking after moving in. And believe me, that happens often.

The reservation fee, which locks the apartment under your name, is 2,000 euros plus VAT. The minimum down payment is 30% of the price before VAT, which equals 32,250 euros in cash for a 107,500 flat before the bank covers the rest. We covered saving for the deposit separately in our guide on apartment down payments.
The full costs, from VAT and notary fees to furnishing, are detailed in our guide on all costs of a new apartment. You can find everything there, complete with examples.

sections.h2: Why prices vary from unit to unit in the same building

blocks.x: In a building with 33 apartments, not all cost the same. Far from it. The difference comes down to three factors.

The floor. Lower-floor units are usually cheaper. Upper-floor units, offering better views and more natural light, cost more. At Ilioara, the lower floors sold first, and the remaining units are on floors 6 and 7, right where the view is at its best.

Surface area. Two rooms can mean 47 square meters or 65. Layout matters as well: a modular apartment that you can adapt to your lifestyle holds more value than one with rigid walls that do not suit you.
Orientation and hallway position. A unit facing the inner courtyard and another facing the street are not identical, even with the same room count. Ask about orientation before looking at the price.

sections.h2: New build versus old build: what you actually gain

blocks.x: A 2-room apartment in an old building in Bucharest may be 15,000 to 20,000 euros cheaper to buy. It seems like a deal. Then come the hidden costs: thermal insulation, rewiring and plumbing replaced piece by piece, 40-year-old pipes, and drafty windows.

In a new building you pay more upfront, but you receive modern insulation, new installations, high-performance windows, and an individual boiler to control your consumption. Five years down the line, utility savings cover part of that price difference.

The number of neighbors on your landing also matters. A short hallway with four units per floor means less foot traffic, more quiet, and fewer building management headaches. It is not a luxury detail. It is something that defines your everyday life.

faq.q: How much does a 2-room apartment in Bucharest cost in 2026?
faq.a: In a new development in District 3, prices start at 107,500 EUR without VAT and reach 136,500 EUR without VAT, depending on floor and surface area. With 21% VAT, the actual total starts at around 130,000 euros. It is a notable investment, but you get a fully finished home.

faq.q: What does the price of a new apartment actually include?
faq.a: It depends on the developer. At Ilioara Residence, the price includes underfloor heating, Salamander triple glazing, and an Ariston boiler. In other projects, these may be paid extras. Ask for clear written terms, not casual promises.

faq.q: Is it better to buy in a new building or an older one?
faq.a: An older building seems cheaper upfront, but it entails renovation costs, outdated plumbing and wiring, and heat loss. A new build costs more initially, but offers modern insulation, brand-new systems, and an individual boiler for full control. Over five years, the math pays off.

faq.q: What is the down payment for a 2-room apartment?
faq.a: At Ilioara, the minimum down payment is 30% of the price before VAT, which equals 32,250 euros for the most affordable unit. The reservation fee is separate at 2,000 EUR plus VAT. Full details are in our down payment guide.
